title: fix(agents): answer replaced by a restated blocker after the plan completion check
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a multi-step turn that ends by asking the user for approval, the answer is replaced (or followed) by a short restatement of the blocker when the run's progress card still has a pending step.

On our setup (Telegram forum topic, `openai/gpt-6-astra`) the topic showed the answer and then a second bubble: "The remaining step is getting the seller's confirmation and quote. That requires your permission to contact them; I haven't sent an enquiry or placed an order." On a Telegram Test Server DM with origin/main, the same shape delivers **only** the restatement. The answer with the actual results never arrives.

## User Impact

A reply that already explains why work stopped (approval, user input, an external dependency) stays the turn's only reply. A plan that the agent genuinely abandoned early still gets the completion check and the agent keeps working. No new messages, notices, or settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause, with provenance:
- #160297 (3ba0a0b2376) added one completion self-check before a run ends with an unfinished saved plan. Its rationale: "an agent can end its reply while its newly saved plan still lists unfinished, authorized work, leaving the session idle. … The built-in agent gets one chance to reconsider that stop: continue feasible work, reconcile the plan, or explain a concrete blocker. This can add one model response."
- The injected check (`attempt-stream-prepare.ts`, `openclaw.plan-completion-check`) tells the model: "If user input, approval, an external dependency, or an explicit pause prevents further work, **report that concrete limitation**." When the stop was legitimate and the reply already asked for approval, the model obeys and writes a fresh report.
- That fresh text becomes the run's final answer (the check continues the same run, and the payload owner uses the latest answer). Non-streamed delivery loses the original answer. When the original was already visible, the user gets a second bubble.
- The gate can't tell a legitimate stop from a premature one. Only the model can, so the decision stays with the model.

Fix: one bounded edit to the existing check text: "…report that concrete limitation; if your previous reply already reported it, end with only `NO_REPLY`." With #164774 (now on main), an answer followed by a `NO_REPLY` stop keeps the earlier answer as the reply. The check's follow-up is a custom message, not user input, so it doesn't reset that answer. Continuing, reconciling, and reporting a blocker that wasn't mentioned all work as before.

Not changed (decisions kept from #160297): the check's gates, its once-per-run budget, cancellation/steering/approval/child/media precedence, and "a checkpoint already shown in chat stays in the conversation".

Rejected alternative: skipping the check when an answer was already delivered or kept. Without deferred terminal delivery the stop answer is already visible on streaming channels, so that would turn the check off there. It also depends on the response's split shape, not on whether the work is done.

## Evidence

Live: Telegram Test Server DM, isolated gateway, real `openai/gpt-6-astra` over `openai-responses` through a forwarding proxy (forwards and logs only), Telegram `streaming.progress` with `toolProgress` + `commentary` (as on our setup). Prompt: "tidy your workspace with a three-step progress card: list files, report sizes, delete the largest; do steps 1–2, ask me before deleting." Bubble counts are the recorder's SUT `message` rows after the sent message, excluding the progress draft that is deleted when the answer lands.

| | origin/main d7f9ebd8de66 (includes #164774) | this PR 807e2cbcb45e |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model answer (transcript) | file table (23 files, sizes) + "**Do you explicitly approve deleting `BOOTSTRAP.md`?**" | file table (23 files, sizes) + "Do you explicitly approve deleting `BOOTSTRAP.md`?" |
| `openclaw.plan-completion-check` injected | yes | yes |
| Model reply to the check | "Step 3 remains pending: deleting `BOOTSTRAP.md` (7,479 bytes) requires your explicit approval. Your latest message does not grant it, so nothing has been deleted. Do you approve deleting `BOOTSTRAP.md`?" (53 output tokens) | `NO_REPLY` (6 output tokens) |
| SUT messages in Telegram after the progress draft retires | 1: **the restatement only** (199 chars), no file table | 1: **the original answer** (1,396 chars) with the file table and the approval question |
| gpt-6-astra requests | 8 | 8 |

#164774 alone doesn't fix this: current main includes it and still delivers only the restatement, because the check's reply is a real answer, not `NO_REPLY`.

#160297's intent still holds, live on this PR head 807e2cbcb45e. Prompt: three file steps, "do the work yourself, without subagents. Do step 1 only, then end this reply with a one-line checkpoint; steps 2 and 3 are authorized and required". The model stopped with "Checkpoint: 1/3 complete—`notes/a.txt` contains exactly `alpha` (5 bytes)…; steps 2 and 3 remain pending." The check was injected. The model then read, wrote `notes/b.txt`, verified, completed the card (3/3), and answered "All 3 steps complete and committed … Total file content in `notes/`: 9 bytes". Telegram showed exactly one SUT message: that final answer. The checkpoint never reached chat on its own.

Regression (`attempt-plan-completion.test.ts`, real session loop + real progress-card tool + payload builder): the stand-in model restates the blocker unless the check text offers silence, which matches the live behavior above. It fails without this change (payload is the restatement) and passes with it (payload is the original answer). `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-plan-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on 807e2cbcb45e: 21 passed, 34.5 s local.

LOC vs origin/main: production +1/−2 (one string, reformatted), docs +3/−2, tests +66.

Review: a fresh adversarial `reviewer` pass (gpt-6-astra) on 807e2cbcb45e, after the rebase onto main, returned `VERDICT: LAND` with no findings.

## Bounded cost

- Same request count as before: the check still costs exactly one follow-up model response per run. In the live runs above both sides made 8 gpt-6-astra requests; the check's reply dropped from 53 to 6 output tokens.
- No new requests, timers, state, or settings; the check text grows by one clause (~15 tokens) only on runs that already get the check.

<details>
<summary>Not the progress narrator</summary>

The stray text is the main model's reply to the injected check (transcript seq after `openclaw.plan-completion-check`, plus its `delivery-mirror` row). Telegram never wires `onNarrationUpdate`, so the utility-model narrator can't post there. A separate burst of ~40 utility-model calls after a reply in an earlier proof run was the gateway Activity recap paging a seeded backlog (`src/gateway/session-activity-summaries.ts`, `MAX_CALLS_PER_HOUR = 40`). It is unrelated to this PR.
</details>
